Day Ashok S. Kinagi J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) challenging the judgment and award dated 12.03.2019 passed in MVC No.687/2016 by the Court of II Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi,
(hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short).

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

3. The facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 25.03.2016 at about 6.00 p.m., at Bankur village cross road, petitioner was proceeding on motorcycle towards Shahabad village.

At that time, a lorry tipper bearing registration No.KA-32/B-8048, being driven NC:
2024:KHC-K:3861-DB by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to the hospital for more than three months.
A criminal case was registered in Crime No.48/2016.

It is contended that the petitioner was hale and healthy as on the date of the accident and working as Medical Practitioner and agriculturist and earning Rs.2,88,658/- per annum and Rs.75,000/- per annum respectively.
It is contended that after the incident, the petitioner is unable to perform his regular duty and he has put to financial loss.
Hence, on these grounds he preferred a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act, seeking compensation.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.1-owner did not appear and placed ex-parte.

Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim petition and it is contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident thereby policy NC: 2024:KHC-K:3861-DB conditions are violated and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

sentences.text: The petitioner, in order to claim, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and also examined one doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P22.
On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurer has not lead any oral evidence as the policy is admitted.

7. The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence allowed the petition in part with cost and it is ordered that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,34,100/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

It is ordered that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation and directed the respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of passing of the award.
The petitioner, NC: 2024:KHC-K:3861-DB aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the tribunal has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

8. Heard the learned counsel for appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
9.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the petitioner has produced the income tax records marked as Exs.P17 to P20 and last income tax returns paid by the petitioner is for the assessment year 2015-16, which discloses that the petitioner has shown his income at Rs.4,18,793/-.

He further submits that the trial Court has not considered the income tax returns produced by the petitioner and assessed the notional income @ Rs.10,000/- per month, which is contrary to the records produced by the petitioner and she also submits that the compensation awarded under other heads is on lower side.
Hence, on the these grounds she prays to allow the appeal.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company supports the judgment and award passed by the tribunal contending that the same does not call for any interference.
Hence, on these grounds she prays to dismiss the appeal.
11. Perused the records and considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The point that arises for our consideration is with regard to quantum.

12. There is no dispute that the petitioner met with an accident and sustained injuries and further in order to prove that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner has produced Ex.P1, the certified copy of FIR and Ex.P3, the certified copy of charge sheet, which discloses that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3861-DB accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

13. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, though the petitioner was working as Medical Practitioner and he was earning Rs.2,88,668/- and in the year 2015-16, he was having income of Rs.4,18,793/-.

In order to substantiate the claim of the petitioner, the petitioner examined himself Dr.Dasrath S/O Ambadas Zingade vs Sharnappa And Anr on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48881517/
3 as PW.1 and he has reiterated the claim petition in the examination-in-chief.
In order to prove the accident, he has produced the records marked as Exs.P17 to P20.

Insofar as the disability is concerned, the petitioner has examined the doctor as PW.2, who has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 42.5%, however the tribunal has assessed the disability at 14%.
We have perused the evidence of PW.2 and also the disability certificate issued by PW.2, which discloses that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
Considering, the evidence of PW.2 and disability certificate, we hold that the disability NC: 2024:KHC-K:3861-DB assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, we assessed 18% disability.

14. As observed above, the petitioner was an income-tax assessee and he has produced the income tax returns, which are marked as Exs.P1 to P20, which discloses that the petitioner was as an income tax assessee and for the financial year 2015-16 the income of the petitioner is shown as Rs.4,18,793/- per annum.
Considering the income tax records for the assessment year 2015-16, we assess the income of the petitioner at Rs.4,18,793/- per annum.

If the said income is divided by 12,
then it comes to Rs.34,899/- per month.
The petitioner is aged about 42 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '16' which is rightly taken by the tribunal.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,06,109/- (Rs.34,899/- x 12 x 18 x 18%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3861-DB 15.

Considering the evidence of PW.2 and disability certificate, we re-assess the compensation under the following heads as under;
Sl. Heads By Tribunal By this Court No.
1. Pain and sufferings Rs.75,000/- Rs.1,50,000/-
2. Attendant, food and Rs.25,000/- Rs.50,000/-
 conveyance charges 3.

Loss of future income Rs.2,68,000/- Rs.12,06,109/-
4.

Medical expenditure Rs.2,80,300/- Rs.2,80,300/-
5. Loss of income during Rs.60,000/- Rs.2,09,394/-
 treatment 6. Loss of amenities and Rs.25,000/- Rs.75,000/-
 nutrition food
The petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.19,70,803/- as against Rs.7,34,100/- awarded by the tribunal.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.12,36,703/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
17.

Hence, we proceed to pass the following:

- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3861-DB (b) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
